source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — North Macedonia ATM/POS/branch series
why_relevant: The single most important cross-country normalised source for MK ATM and POS-terminal counts: FAS collects country-wide ATM numbers (search results indicate 1,041 MK ATMs in 2024 vs 1,023 in 2023) plus POS terminals disaggregated rural/urban, on an annual cycle with an October release. Because the underlying reporter is NBRSM, FAS also functions as an independent audit trail on MK-published counts.

source_name: DBnomics — IMF/FAS mirror (free machine-readable aggregator)
why_relevant: Free, open, API-first mirror of IMF FAS (and many other providers), which removes the licensing and bot-defence friction of CEIC/Trading Economics for the same underlying ATM/POS/access series. Best low-cost substitute for a paid aggregator.

source_name: FRED (St. Louis Fed) — Geographical Outreach: Number of ATMs, Country Wide for Macedonia (MKDFCACNUM)
why_relevant: A named, stable series ID for MK country-wide ATM counts (FAS-derived), with a free API, CSV export and revision history. Ideal machine-collectable anchor for the ATM component of the cell.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex 2025 — North Macedonia microdata and country data
why_relevant: Only comparable demand-side source on MK adults' account ownership, card ownership and use, digital payment frequency, and cash reliance — the demand-side counterpart to NBRSM's supply-side card/POS counts, and the evidentiary basis for any 'cash usage' claim. 2025 wave covers 141 economies including MK, with downloadable microdata.

source_name: TheGlobalEconomy.com — North Macedonia ATM machines and financial indicators
why_relevant: Free, scrape-friendly re-presentation of WB/IMF MK banking and ATM indicators with ready-made country rankings; useful for quick peer-ranking checks and for spotting which MK indicators have been discontinued upstream. Derivative, so never a primary citation.

source_name: World Bank — Western Balkans Payments Modernization Project (with RCC and CEFTA Secretariat, EC-funded)
why_relevant: The central regional programme on WB6 payments modernisation and integration, jointly run with RCC and the CEFTA Secretariat under the Common Regional Market agenda. Its diagnostics, country annexes and workshop materials are the richest regional source of MK payments benchmarking (cost of payments, interoperability, cross-border retail payments) and a snowball hub to further studies, consultants and named counterparts at NBRSM.

source_name: Regional Cooperation Council (RCC) — Common Regional Market / Digital Transformation publications
why_relevant: RCC's CRM and Regional Digital Area workstreams generate comparative WB6 studies, action-plan monitoring reports and a documents library (crm_docs) that repeatedly touch e-commerce, digital payments and financial-services integration — a reliable snowball hub for MK-relevant regional evidence and for identifying which institutions hold the underlying data.

source_name: CEFTA Secretariat — trade facilitation, digitalisation and e-commerce work programme
why_relevant: CEFTA's 2026 priorities centre on trade facilitation, digitalisation and reducing business barriers across WB6; its e-commerce and digital-payments strands (co-run with RCC and the World Bank) produce comparative studies and Joint Committee decisions that document MK-specific frictions in cross-border card and e-commerce payments.

source_name: NBRSM press release — Western Balkans payment systems modernisation and regional interlinking (Banca d'Italia / ECB supported)
source_subtype: central bank press release (pointer to regional programme)
why_relevant: Found only via Macedonian-language search. Documents MK's participation in the ECB/Banca d'Italia-backed regional payment-system interlinking initiative — the MK-side entry point to a regional programme whose analytical outputs are the comparator material this cell needs. Also names the institutional counterparts to track.

source_name: Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje — quarterly investor presentations (PDF series)
why_relevant: Analyst-facing decks from the largest MK bank, published on a stable, guessable URL pattern (KB-PRESENTATION-DDMMYYYY[-ENG].pdf) each quarter. They carry market-share tables, card portfolio and channel/digital-banking indicators that are not in aggregate statistics, and constitute the commercial-analyst layer for MK. The predictable filename pattern makes them ideal for scheduled collection and for Wayback back-filling of withdrawn editions.

source_name: TheBanks.eu — Macedonia country profile and major banks league table
why_relevant: Third-party commercial aggregator that normalises MK bank balance-sheet data into a ranked league table with market shares (e.g. Komercijalna ~192.60bn MKD / 20.61% and Stopanska ~157.22bn MKD / 16.82% for 2025 per its pages). Useful for fast market-structure framing that would otherwise require assembling individual bank reports.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — North Macedonia / Western Balkans financial-sector coverage and rating-action archive
why_relevant: Commercial regional business-intelligence outlet that reports rating actions on MK (e.g. the Fitch downgrade to 'BB' during the political crisis) and bank/payments developments in the Western Balkans, often summarising analyst reports that are otherwise paywalled. Serves as an early-warning and pointer layer into rating-agency and consultancy output.

source_name: Consultancy market-report vendors covering MK e-commerce and payments (Mordor Intelligence, ResearchAndMarkets, Verified Market Research)
why_relevant: These vendors publish MK-specific e-commerce/payments sizing and payment-method mix that circulate widely as the de facto commercial view (e.g. cards ~46% of 2024 e-commerce payment share with wallets growing fast; cash-on-delivery cited at ~70% of purchases; MK e-commerce ~USD 0.6bn in 2024). Their table-of-contents and sample pages are free and reveal which underlying MK sources they rely on — valuable as pointers even when the report itself is unaffordable.

source_name: Payments-industry vendor explainers on MK local payment methods (Transfi, PayAtlas, EcommerceBridge)
why_relevant: PSP-facing country guides that enumerate MK acquirers, card schemes accepted, local payment methods, compliance requirements and fee norms — operational detail absent from official statistics. They also carry recent market claims (MK e-commerce EUR 213m in Q1 2025, cross-border shopping +32%, digital transactions +21% in 2024) that flag where to look for primary confirmation.

source_name: Bruegel — Western Balkans working papers (intra-regional economic integration)
why_relevant: Independent think-tank analysis of intra-Western-Balkans integration provides the analytical framing and comparator datasets used by EU institutions when assessing MK; free full-text PDFs make it a low-friction substitute for paywalled consultancy work.

source_name: eKupi.mk — Начини за плаќање (payment-methods page)
why_relevant: One of the largest MK e-commerce platforms; its payment-methods and instalment pages disclose the acquiring bank, card schemes accepted, 3DS redirect host and interest-free instalment partners — a direct read on e-commerce acquiring share.

source_name: Literatura.mk — Начини на плаќање
why_relevant: Typical MK online merchant page that names the acquiring bank (Stopanska Banka / NBG) and the processor (CaSys) explicitly; useful as a template example and as one datapoint in an acquirer-mapping census of MK webshops.

source_name: КРШ (krs.mk) — Плаќање со платежни картички
why_relevant: Retail merchant card-payment page; another acquirer/PSP disclosure datapoint for the webshop census.

source_name: Форма Нова (formanova.com.mk) — Начини на плаќање
why_relevant: Furniture retail chain webshop payment page; instalment-card and acquirer disclosure.

source_name: nama.mk — Начини на плаќање
why_relevant: Department-store style MK retailer; payment-methods page contributes to the acquirer/PSP census.

source_name: Скопска.мк — Skopje public-transport ticketing (JSP / Skopska card & app)
why_relevant: Official portal of the Skopje public-transport contactless ticketing scheme (SKOPSKA card, virtual card, mobile app, validators). Discloses ticketing technology, top-up channels and card-acceptance evolution in urban transit — the largest single MK contactless-acceptance deployment outside retail.

source_name: Sitel — JSP tariff / Skopska card and mobile payment coverage
why_relevant: National broadcaster reporting on JSP fare/payment-channel changes; useful as an event feed for transit payment milestones when the operator itself publishes little.

source_name: Радио МОФ / Слободен печат / Нова Македонија — transit and utility payment-channel reporting
why_relevant: Independent MK outlets that consistently cover launches of new payment channels by municipal utilities and transit operators (virtual bus card, water-bill web payment, parking apps) — a practical event feed for acceptance-side milestones.

source_name: ЈП Водовод и канализација Скопје — е-услуги / Брзо плаќање
why_relevant: Municipal water utility's card-payment portal for Skopje; shows which acquirer/gateway handles the largest municipal biller in the country and whether commission-free card payment is offered — a direct indicator of bill-payment migration away from cash/counters.

source_name: ЕВН Home онлајн услуги (evnonline.mk)
why_relevant: The electricity supplier is the single largest recurring biller in MK; its online portal's card-payment terms (commission-free, accepted brands, gateway) are a strong proxy for household card-on-file and e-payment adoption.

source_name: ЈП Водовод и канализација Прилеп — Плати сметка
why_relevant: Regional (non-Skopje) municipal utility card-payment page — evidence of how far e-payment acceptance has spread beyond the capital, and which small-market gateway serves regional public enterprises.

source_name: Македонски Телеком — М-TAG електронска наплата на патарина
why_relevant: Telecom-operated distribution of the national electronic toll device; shows the toll payment scheme (M-TAG device, M-Card contactless smart card), pricing, top-up channels and retail distribution through telecom shops — a distinct closed-loop prepaid instrument competing with open-loop cards.

source_name: Македонски Телеком — Општи услови за онлајн нарачка и плаќање (PDF)
why_relevant: Terms document for the largest telecom's webshop — typically names the acquiring bank, accepted card schemes, 3DS provider and refund flow; one of the few written disclosures of an enterprise acquiring relationship in MK.
